deviations.qemu_behavior: Recalled from QEMU's backends/tpm and hw/tpm sources, not re-read for this entry: TIS reset runs on every machine reset, including the initial one, and power-cycles the swtpm (tpm-emulator) backend with CMD_INIT before the guest runs; a failed CMD_INIT power cycle is reported and QEMU exits. The data socket has no read timeout. A failed exchange is answered by tpm_util_write_fatal_error_response with a 10-byte TPM 1.2-format response (tag 0x00C4, TPM_FAIL), and the next command uses the same socket again.
deviations.bridgevm_behavior: Reset power cycles match QEMU: with a control socket configured, every helper generation that boots its guest sends one CMD_INIT before it creates the VM, and every in-process guest reboot sends another. A failed CMD_INIT at helper start stops the helper before the VM exists, so no vCPU runs (a stop line, exit status 1). A checkpoint restore, which product runs cannot request, connects without CMD_INIT, and checkpoints carry no TPM state. The swtpm data and control sockets have 30 s timeouts. The first I/O error on either socket (timeout, short read, broken pipe) or swtpm response whose declared size is outside 10..=4096 bytes latches the backend failed and prints one stderr line. Neither socket is read or written again: that command and every later one complete through the TIS FIFO with the TPM 2.0 response 80 01 00 00 00 0a 00 00 01 01 (TPM_ST_NO_SESSIONS, TPM_RC_FAILURE), and every later backend reset fails without sending CMD_INIT. Commands refused before any socket I/O (a locality other than 0, a malformed command) fail without latching. When the backend reset for an in-process guest reboot fails, because CMD_INIT was rejected or the backend had already latched, the probe stops through its fatal reset path (a stop line, exit status 1) before any device is reset, instead of panicking.
deviations.impact: A swtpm stall longer than 30 s, which QEMU would wait out, fails the rest of the helper process's TPM commands, and the failure code differs from QEMU's TPM_FAIL. The next in-process guest reboot then stops the VM where QEMU would reboot after a successful CMD_INIT. Product runs set BRIDGEVM_EXIT_ON_RESET=1, so a guest reset starts a new helper process, which reconnects and power-cycles swtpm or stops before creating the VM. The guest no longer receives a response that belongs to another command. Before acae6e96 (2026-10-23) that new helper connected without CMD_INIT, so a product guest reboot kept the previous boot's volatile TPM state, including PCRs, and TPM2_Startup(CLEAR) failed with TPM_RC_INITIALIZE (shown against a real swtpm, not with a guest); this registry did not record that difference. Evidence is deterministic socket-pair, scripted-socket and injected-backend tests plus one real swtpm 0.10.1 test of two helper generations; no Windows guest, BitLocker or PPI run has exercised this behaviour.
